subject: Re: Follow-up on SUP-19288 — regional degradation + automatic failover behavior
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@northwind.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@northwind.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 20, 2025 at 4:42 PM PT
Subject: Re: Follow-up on SUP-19288 — regional degradation + automatic failover behavior

Maya, Raj — following up on SUP-19288.

First: thanks for the detailed request IDs and timestamps your team shared. It materially shortened our investigation. As discussed on the call, the symptom you saw (intermittent routing into a degraded region with elevated tail latency/timeouts) is exactly the failure mode we’re targeting with our current reliability work.

Below is a concrete summary of (a) what we’re changing, (b) what you should expect when a region is partially impaired vs hard down, and (c) how to escalate with the fastest path.

1) What reliability improvements are in progress (and why it matters)
We are upgrading regional failover from largely manual/heuristic steps to an auditable, safety-guarded automation path. This work is underway now and is being rolled out in stages.

Key changes:
- Standardized region health signals (aggregated):
  - error rate (5xx/429), tail latency (p95/p99), dependency health, capacity saturation, and network path health.
  - goal: earlier detection of “brownout” conditions (packet loss / elevated tail) before it becomes customer-visible.

- Central trigger evaluation + hysteresis (to avoid flappy failovers):
  - trigger windows + hold-down timers
  - multi-signal gating (we won’t fail over on a single noisy metric)

- “Safe-to-failover” checks before we move traffic:
  - target-region capacity headroom (GPU pool + queue depth)
  - dependency readiness (e.g., routing policy store / auth / logging path)
  - sanity checks to prevent a bad config from pushing traffic to an unsafe destination

- Progressive failover (rather than all-at-once):
  - canary percentage first, then expand
  - scoped by route/model/customer tier where appropriate

- Clear audit trail:
  - when/why the system would have triggered
  - what checks passed/failed
  - who approved/overrode (where manual approval is required)

2) What you should expect during regional impairment
We want to set expectations clearly: the goal is “degraded but available” rather than hard failure, and to reduce time-to-mitigation. That said, during partial impairment there are trade-offs.

If a region is degraded but not fully down, you may see:
- brief increases in latency while routing policies rebalance
- increased retries on some requests (client-side retry behavior can amplify this; we can review your current settings)
- temporary rate limiting / load shedding for lower-priority traffic to protect system stability
- for streaming: intermittent disconnects if the network path is impaired (we’re adding additional detection for this class)

If a region crosses the failover threshold and safe-to-failover checks pass, you may see:
- traffic routed to another region for the affected routes
- a short period of elevated latency during DNS/edge propagation (we are designing for conservative TTLs and rollback)
- possible model-variant fallback if the exact variant is constrained in the target region (only when configured; we will not silently change behavior for Dedicated customers without agreement)

For Dedicated capacity specifically:
- automatic regional failover is opt-in per environment and requires pre-arranged capacity or an explicit burst agreement in the target region.
- in other words: we can’t safely “swing” Dedicated workloads into a region that doesn’t have the reserved headroom.

3) Timeline / rollout stance
We are not asking you to “trust the automation” blind.

Current state (today):
- The new trigger logic is running in monitor-only mode for selected scopes (it evaluates and records what it would do, without moving traffic).

Near-term:
- Controlled failover tests (low-risk slices) with explicit go/no-go criteria and rollback plans.
- After we validate signal quality and guardrails, we expand coverage.

If helpful, I can share the specific scope we’re targeting for your routes (hosted vs dedicated) and what would be required to enable automated failover on your Dedicated deployment.

4) Escalation paths (fastest way to get help)
If you see recurrence of the symptoms from SUP-19288:
- Open a Support ticket and tag it Sev-1 (or Sev-2 if you can tolerate degraded performance).
- Include:
  - 3–5 representative request IDs
  - time range + timezone
  - affected region(s) if known
  - whether it’s streaming vs non-streaming
  - your client retry/timeouts settings (if changed recently)

For urgent escalation:
- Use the emergency escalation mechanism in your Enterprise Support portal (that pages our on-call SRE directly).
- You can also reference “SUP-19288 follow-up” so it routes to the same on-call context.

We will continue to post regional impact updates to the status page (status.redwoodinference.com). For controlled tests, we will provide advance notice and a brief post-test summary.

Attachment: a short one-pager we’ve been sending to enterprise customers summarizing failover behaviors and what’s configurable.

If you want, we can set up a 30-minute working session next week with your infra/app owner to review:
- your current region pinning preferences
- retry/timeout guidance for streaming vs non-streaming
- what “opt-in” failover would look like for your Dedicated deployment

Regards,
Sean

Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Multi-Region_Failover_Overview_Mar2025.pdf

From: Maya Chen <maya.chen@northwind.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@northwind.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 20, 2025 at 6:03 PM PT
Subject: Re: Follow-up on SUP-19288 — regional degradation + automatic failover behavior

Sean — thanks, this is helpful and the level of specificity is what we needed.

Two questions:
1) For Dedicated, can we configure “fail over only on hard down” (vs brownout), to avoid bouncing regions for transient latency spikes?
2) If model-variant fallback is possible in the target region, can we lock it down to a defined allowlist? We have some eval constraints and don’t want surprises.

We’d like to take you up on the working session. Raj can join as well.

Maya

Maya Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
Northwind Analytics

---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@northwind.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@northwind.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Mar 21, 2025 at 9:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Follow-up on SUP-19288 — regional degradation + automatic failover behavior

Maya — yes to both, with a bit of nuance:

1) Dedicated: “hard down only” vs brownout triggers
- We can configure thresholds so that Dedicated failover requires a stronger signal set (e.g., sustained high 5xx + dependency/path failure) rather than pure tail-latency degradation.
- We still recommend keeping a brownout mitigation mode enabled (e.g., controlled load shedding, tightened timeouts, and/or partial routing adjustments) so you don’t get stuck in a prolonged degraded state while waiting for a “hard down” condition.
- In practice we’ll propose: (a) brownout actions that do not move 100% of traffic cross-region, and (b) failover only when the region is genuinely unhealthy and stable under the hold-down window.

2) Model fallback allowlist
- Completely aligned. For enterprise/Dedicated we treat fallback as an explicit policy.
- We can lock to an allowlist (e.g., exact model version only, or exact + one compatible variant you approve), and we can also configure “no fallback allowed” so it fails closed if capacity is constrained.

For the working session: can you send 2–3 time windows that work Tue–Thu next week? If you share your current region preferences + model/version pins in advance, we’ll come prepared with a recommended policy draft.

Thanks,
Sean
